findings.description: External pull() on dispatcher hook (and ERC1155 transfer) executes inside _syncBudget/stake/unstake before reward-accounting state writes; classic state-change-after-external-call. Mitigated by OZ nonReentrant on all entry points, but the cross-function ordering is flagged. Aderyn HIGH (state change after external call, NFTStaker.sol:445) corroborates.
Same pull()-before-state-write pattern as NFTStaker, on the priceScale-multiplier copy (story-017 focus contract). nonReentrant-guarded. Aderyn HIGH at NFTStakerPriceScaled.sol:484 corroborates.
Same pull()-before-state-write pattern, plus depositFor and migration entry points. nonReentrant-guarded. Aderyn HIGH at NFTStakerDepletion.sol:554 and :771 corroborate.

migrateIn loops over parked users calling staker.depositFor(user, amt) as an external interaction; Aderyn HIGH flags state writes at :205/:226. NOTE: per-user effects (parked[user]=0, totalParked-=amt, _removeParked) are applied BEFORE the depositFor call (CEI honoured), function is onlyOwner + nonReentrant, and the external target is the trusted immutable staker. Low real exploitability; surfaced for the loop+external-call shape and corroboration.

Return value of nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient) ignored at L281, and tuple destructure of configs() at L249 drops fields. If mint() returns a status/minted-id that callers rely on, the dropped value could mask a partial/failed mint inside the batch loop. Worth a look at whether the minted token id is needed downstream.

Tuple destructure of nftMinter.configs(dispatcherIndex) intentionally ignores fields other than price/growthBasisPoints (per spec latestPrice = price/r). Likely intended; flagged for completeness. Same pattern in NFTStakerPriceScaled._recomputeSchedule (L421).

Loop accumulators (total, count) declared without explicit init (default 0). Benign in 0.8.x (zero-default), accumulation is correct. Same shape in NFTStakerDepletion.batchMigrate (totalAmount L696) and NFTStakerMigrator.migrate (total L84, migratedCount L99) and BatchNFTMinter (nudgeAmount L272). QA-level.
Strict equality begin == 0 used as a not-parked sentinel. Benign null-check (false positive in the dangerous-equality sense); kept as low-confidence per recall.
Strict equality rewardRate == 0 guards against div-by-zero in V/R runway math. Benign guard, not a manipulable equality. Kept low-confidence.

findings.function: _updatePool / _recomputeSchedule / unstake / emergencyWithdraw / claimTimedOut / claimableAt and reward/runway views
findings.description: block.timestamp drives reward accrual (lastRewardTime/windowEnd elapsed math), runway = V/R windows, and the migration timeout escape hatch (migrationBegin + migrationTimeout). NOT dropped: these protocols are explicitly time-driven, so timestamp logic is load-bearing (emission stop at windowEnd, depletion duration, timeout gating). Miner +/- seconds skew is negligible vs the windows but the dependency is real and central to correctness. Forwarded for dedup/severity to weigh.

External calls performed inside unbounded loops (staker.depositFor per parked user; nftMinter.mint per batch item; payouts in batchMigrate). DoS / out-of-gas exposure if the caller-supplied array or parked-user set is large; all are owner-gated batch operations so the owner controls batch size, but an over-sized batch is a footgun (must be chunked). Aderyn corroborates as costly-ops/loop on InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator and NFTStakerDepletion.
